items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Teddy went in and as Yank was very well liked by Barney Josepson, Teddy was obliged to use him.

ctx.x: We didn't play loud because it was not necessary. Teddy had a soft when touch on piano, Benny Morton was at his best/playing not too loud and so was I. That was the big difference in playing in a big band and a small combo. In a big band you must blow loud and my ideas and technique were not as good when I had to play loud. Hamilton had a nice soft sound on clarinet and was really an admirer of Benny Goodman. So Yank's brushing style was nice for the band except as I mentioned before, it didn't always give the…

Yank Porter had worked at a Cafe before. Teddy went in and as Yank was very well liked by Barney Josepson, Teddy was obliged to use him. And John Hammond had made pressure on him to hire me, although I had worked with Teddy in Benny Carter's orchestra, I know that he had another trumpet player in mind when I was pushed on him.

Teddy was quite a nice person but I soon found out that he had a sunny character because we used to play a certain number in which he would play his solo in a minor key and the number and other solos were in major. I liked the way Teddy made it sound in minor and one night I asked him if I could play my solo also in minor. He told me yes, but after I had taken my solo, he did not play his, and then I knew that he didn't like it because I had played it in minor. I never asked to do it in minor again.
